items.hook: The 1997 Alon-Kim conjecture on edge-coloring hypergraphs is proved.
items.summary: The authors prove that hypergraphs whose edges pairwise share at most t vertices can be edge-colored with about (t-1+1/t) times the maximum degree colors, as Alon and Kim conjectured. The proof combines convex optimization with probabilistic methods. The bound is asymptotic, so it holds only once the maximum degree is sufficiently large, and it is a preprint not yet refereed.
items.title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture

items.hook: The Berry phase appears as the first correction in the minimal action of slowly driven oscillators.
items.summary: For a one-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian system whose parameters change slowly around a loop, the paper shows the minimal action has an expansion in the slowness whose first coefficient is the classical Berry phase. The result is proved mathematically for exact convex functions, so no adiabatic approximation is used. The expansions are only asymptotic, not convergent, and the setting is limited to one degree of freedom.
items.title: Berry phase and Hannay angle as Taylor coefficients of the minimal action

items.hook: Pulsations of a star in a binary pin down its mass at 1.594 solar masses and its companion at 1.121.
items.summary: Delta Scuti pulsations seen by TESS identify the primary of the binary HD 70510 and fix its mass and radius, which removes the usual inclination ambiguity of Gaia orbits. Combined with the orbit, this gives an inclination near 82 degrees and a companion of 1.121 solar masses. The intervals depend on the assumed identification of the pulsation modes and on the stellar and SED models.
items.title: Asteroseismology of the Gaia SB2 HD 70510: From Radial Modes to Component Masses

items.hook: Monotone solutions of the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation in 4D depend on one variable only.
items.summary: The paper proves the anisotropic version of De Giorgi's conjecture in four dimensions: monotone entire solutions that tend to plus or minus one at the ends are functions of one variable. It first shows that globally minimizing anisotropic surfaces are halfspaces, then uses a tilt-excess decay estimate and a Liouville argument. The result needs the limiting assumption at infinity and holds only in four dimensions.
items.title: The anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$

items.hook: A halide pretreatment anchors the molecular layer in perovskite solar cells, reaching 27.3% efficiency.
items.summary: The authors find that buried interfaces fail by adhesion loss under temperature swings, and treat the transparent oxide with a metal halide so the self-assembled monolayer binds at many points. Devices reach 27.3 percent efficiency (26.9 certified) and keep 94 percent after 400 cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C. Only small lab cells were tested, and long-term outdoor durability is not shown.
items.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells

items.hook: The essential p-dimension of PGL(p^n) is p^(2n-2)+1, settling a long-open count.
items.summary: The paper determines the essential p-dimension of central simple algebras of degree p^n, giving p^(2n-2)+1 for PGL(p^n), which extends Merkurjev's case n=2. The lower bounds apply a theorem of Ofek to block centralizers. As a consequence, it constructs exponent-p division algebras that stay noncrossed products, but only for degrees p^n with n at least 3 (4 when p=2).
items.title: Essential $p$-dimension of simple algebras and noncrossed products of prime exponent

items.hook: Primes with ||alpha p|| small exist in much shorter intervals than before, down to X^(7/12).
items.summary: The paper shows that for any irrational alpha, short intervals of length X^gamma with gamma above 7/12 contain primes p for which alpha p is very close to an integer, with an asymptotic count. This widens the earlier range of 2/3 to Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals. The result holds for infinitely many X, not every X, and the allowed closeness exponent is small.
items.title: Diophantine approximation with prime denominators in short intervals

items.hook: A lost fifth planet that merged with another may explain Barnard's Star's broken resonant chain.
items.summary: Simulations test whether a vanished extra planet merged with a neighbor to leave the four known sub-Earth planets around Barnard's Star. Two pathways work, tidal expansion driven by the star or early disk-driven expansion, and the second fits 14 similar compact systems, ten of which break the chain at the third planet. This is a dynamical model, and the lost planet is not observed.
items.title: Breaking the Chain: The Dynamical History of the Barnard's Star Planetary System

items.hook: Triconnected percolation clusters have fractal dimension 1.2308 in 2D, falling to zero by 6D.
items.summary: A new algorithm based on SPQR decomposition finds clusters that stay connected after removing any two sites, and Monte Carlo runs estimate their fractal dimension in 2, 3 and 4 dimensions. The dimension drops with dimension and vanishes at 6 and above, so the susceptibility stays finite for d of 3 or more. The values come from finite-size simulations, and the d=6 conclusion rests on logarithmic growth.
items.title: Critical geometry of triconnected clusters in percolation

items.hook: Researchers rewrite an AI-generated proof of the Falconer distance conjecture for graduate readers.
items.summary: This note presents a simplified version of a proof of the Falconer distance conjecture, whose main idea the authors took from a recent OpenAI release. It rewrites the arguments for graduate-level readers. The abstract gives no technical detail, and correctness depends on the underlying AI-produced proof and on community checking, so the claim is unverified here.
items.title: On the proof of Falconer distance conjecture

items.hook: Laser scanning and diamond magnetometry image the modes of a 33-resonator superconducting lattice.

readout.label: Bound on relative on-site frequency disorder

items.summary: Laser scanning microscopy images the eigenmodes of a honeycomb array of 33 resonators, while nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry maps the local microwave magnetic field. Together they confirm the lattice matches its design, show a topological edge state with measured sublattice polarization, and bound on-site frequency disorder at about 0.3 percent. It is one device, and the bound is an upper limit.
items.title: Eigenmode and field imaging of a compact superconducting resonator array

items.hook: A group built from SL2 over Z/p^9 is a counterexample to Kourovka Problem 21.7.
items.summary: The paper proves that the kernel of SL2(Z/p^9) to SL2(F_p) is not IYB, while its product with a cyclic group is, which yields a supersoluble group with IYB Sylow subgroups that is not IYB. The proof rules out a pre-Lie multiplication using three trace identities. It holds for primes above 24, and the smallest odd-order example it names is of order 3 times 31^32.
items.title: A congruence-group counterexample to Kourovka Problem 21.7

items.hook: Photodiode homodyne readout could detect atom-qubit states above 99% fidelity in 100 microseconds
items.summary: The authors propose reading out neutral-atom qubits by mixing the atoms' fluorescence with a reference beam on photodiodes, avoiding slow cameras. An analytic model of atomic motion, checked with 3D Monte Carlo simulation, finds an optimal detection time and predicts fidelity above 99% within 100 microseconds. This is simulation only, with no experiment yet.
items.title: Coherent Optical Readout of Neutral-Atom Qubits via Homodyne Detection of Resonant Fluorescence

items.hook: A 3D-printed ceramic optical bench holds a rubidium frequency reference in just 6 mL

readout.label: Laser fractional frequency instability at 1 s

items.summary: Researchers 3D-print monolithic ceramic optical benches, then align and glue optics onto them to build compact atomic sensors. A rubidium reference in a 6 mL alumina module stabilizes a laser to 3e-12 fractional instability at 1 s. The magnetometer and optical trap are designs or early demonstrators, with performance not yet shown in the field or space.
items.title: Additively manufactured ceramic platforms for miniaturized optical frequency references and robust atomic sensor systems

items.hook: Closed, stress-free martensite nuclei can form inside austenite, built from simple-shear deformations
items.summary: Earlier geometric conditions allow stress-free interfaces between austenite and martensite but do not guarantee they close into a nucleus. The authors identify families of deformations, including simple shear, that give self-accommodating closed martensite islands called elastic Landau states. Predictions match deformations reconstructed from observed microstructures, but that match is suggestive rather than proof of the mechanism.
items.title: Elastic Landau states as martensite nuclei in austenite

items.hook: A real 4x4x4x4 symmetric tensor has rank 10 but symmetric rank 11, breaking Comon's conjecture
items.summary: Comon's conjecture says a symmetric tensor's ordinary rank equals its symmetric rank. The author constructs a fourth-order Hankel tensor in dimension 4 with ranks 10 and 11, and shows direct sums widen the gap without bound. It is a counterexample over the real numbers only, and it is a pure existence result.
items.title: Rank Additivity and Comon's Conjecture for Real Hankel Tensors

items.hook: Dense star clusters relax to one density profile whatever their start, simulations show
items.summary: Monte Carlo simulations with CMC-COSMIC find that clusters of a given mass and binding energy settle into a King profile with W_0=6.8, regardless of initial density. Black hole binaries in the core supply the energy that balances contraction, and the final virial radius is about 7 times the initial. The result comes from simulations, not observed clusters.
items.title: On the Existence of an Equilibrium Density Profile for Massive Collisional Star Clusters

items.hook: Energetic atmospheric muons exceed model predictions in four experiments, echoing the air-shower puzzle
items.summary: Comparing published muon measurements from four experiments with predictions from one hadronic model and cosmic-ray flux, the authors find measurements mostly exceed predictions. The excess is steadier than any trend with energy or angle, pointing to more energetic muon parents rather than more soft particles. It relies on a single model choice and published data, so model uncertainties could shift the result.
items.title: Cross-experiment tests of the atmospheric-muon excess

items.hook: Galaxies seen by JWST at z 9 to 15 suggest star formation fell slowly to z~17, then faster to z~20

readout.label: Median redshift when 20% of mass formed

items.summary: The authors build a model of bursty star formation histories, test it on simulated galaxies, and apply it to 400 JWST galaxies. They infer the galaxies' ages, finding only 28 of 218 formed 20% of their mass by z=15, with a median formation redshift of 16.9. Conclusions at z>15 are extrapolations from model fits, and the z=20 constraint rests on a single galaxy.
items.title: Tracing early galaxies back in time: implications for the dearth of galaxies beyond z~15

items.hook: Only four such maps permute trace-1 elements of a binary field, proving the Hollmann-Xiang conjecture
items.summary: Hollmann and Xiang conjectured which polynomials of the form t plus a linearized map of 1/t permute the trace-1 elements of a binary field. The author proves only four cases work, using moment identities, and also proves a second conjecture about Kloosterman polynomials. This is a classification proof, so it matters mostly to specialists in coding theory and finite fields.
items.title: A Moment Proof of the Hollman-Xiang Conjectures on Kloosterman Polynomials

items.hook: Polya's eigenvalue inequality holds, with a curvature shift, for every ball in hyperbolic space
items.hook_turn: for every ball in hyperbolic space
items.summary: The authors prove a shifted Polya inequality bounding the Dirichlet eigenvalues of geodesic balls in hyperbolic space in every dimension of 2 or more. They also prove a weaker Berezin-Li-Yau type bound for arbitrary finite-volume open sets, and a global estimate proposed by Strichartz. The full Polya inequality is shown for balls only, not general domains.
items.title: P\'olya's conjecture for hyperbolic balls and Berezin--Li--Yau type inequalities

items.hook: An AI model estimates global rain every 15 minutes at 0.1 degrees and beats IMERG, ERA5 and HRES
items.summary: PARDIG is a graph transformer trained on atmospheric analyses and geostationary imagery to predict spaceborne radar rainfall, then applied everywhere. Checks against radar networks in the US, Europe and Japan and over 36,000 stations show gains over IMERG V07, MSWEP V3, ERA5 and HRES, most at extreme rain. Its training targets cover limited radar swaths, so skill in unsampled regimes is less certain.
items.title: PARDIG: Global Precipitation Estimates Learned from Sparse Satellite Observations

items.hook: A text index adds each new letter in constant time and still answers searches in optimal time.
items.hook_turn: still answers searches in optimal time.
items.summary: The authors build the first index for pattern matching over integer alphabets that handles each appended letter in O(1) worst-case time and reports a pattern's occurrences in O(|P|+occ) time. The key is a path-decomposed suffix tree that stores paths in a dictionary instead of the full tree. The constant update time holds only with high probability, and the result is theoretical with no implementation reported.
items.title: Real-Time String Indexing in Optimal Time

items.hook: NGC 4569's gas tail dates its stripping by the Virgo Cluster to about 250 million years ago.
items.summary: A fast orbit-reconstruction model fits the positions and velocities of the galaxy and 94 Halpha regions, plus cluster gravity and hot gas density, to find when ram pressure peaked (about 163 Myr ago). The galaxy's line-of-sight distance is unknown, so the fit splits into a pre-peak and a post-peak branch, and only an independent stripping-radius check favors the post-peak one. Results depend on that assumed distance and on a spherical cluster model.
items.title: A Virgo Environmental Survey Tracing Ionised Gas Emission (VESTIGE). XXIII. NGC 4569 past orbit reconstruction with ORFEO

items.hook: Models predict making element 120 with titanium-50 beams yields only about 18 femtobarns.
items.summary: Using a dinuclear system model, the study estimates how often titanium-50 beams on berkelium-249 or californium-249 would produce elements 119 and 120, and predicts their alpha-decay chains. The peak cross sections sit well below the upper limits set by earlier GSI experiments. It is a calculation tuned to one measured reaction, and other nuclear mass tables give values up to 25 times smaller.
items.title: Formation of superheavy elements 119 and 120 in the $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk and $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Cf reactions: dinuclear system dynamics, survival probability, and decay chains of the evaporation residues

items.hook: The coldest neutron stars rule out muon-driven baryon decay far below what labs can reach.
items.hook_turn: far below what labs can reach.
items.summary: If an interaction turns muons and protons into dark baryons, neutron stars would heat up or collapse. The author computes the conversion rate, the heat released, and how a star evolves, then compares with the coldest known stars. The bounds rest on theoretical modeling of dense matter, and avoiding collapse depends on how strongly dark baryons repel each other, which is assumed.
items.title: Neutron stars nearly close the window for muon-induced baryon-number violation

items.hook: A player can build a triangle factor in a semi-random graph in at most 2.929329n rounds.

readout.label: Upper bound to build a triangle factor

items.summary: In a game where random vertices are offered and the player picks partners, the authors give a strategy that covers all vertices with disjoint triangles within 2.929329n rounds with high probability. This is a proof of an upper bound by analysis of a specific strategy. It does not show the bound is the best possible.
items.title: Triangle Factors in the Semi-Random Graph Process

items.hook: Words carry speech at the lowest bitrate, with slightly longer units sometimes doing better.
items.hook_turn: with slightly longer units sometimes doing better.
items.summary: Using 960 hours of transcribed English audiobooks, the study compares how many bits per second are needed to encode speech as phones, syllables, words, and multi-word chunks. Both n-gram and transformer language models were used under limited capacity. Results come from one language and read speech, and depend on the modeling budget chosen.
items.title: On the information rate of phones, syllables and words

items.hook: Pulse-based deepfake detectors do not detect a pulse. They pick up high-frequency video artifacts.
items.hook_turn: They pick up high-frequency video artifacts.

readout.label: AUC of chrominance traces, talking-face fakes

items.summary: Tests on Celeb-DF++ and FaceForensics++ show simple color traces beat a dedicated pulse extractor, yet work equally well on backgrounds and sit above the heart-rate band. Detectors trained on one dataset label over 99% of real videos from the other as fake, and the Celeb-DF splits leak identities between training and test. The findings cover two datasets and the detector families tested.
items.title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn

items.hook: Frege's election method settles into a finite polygon attractor, mapped by Farey fractions for three parties.
items.summary: The authors treat a proportional seat-allocation rule as a dynamical system. For almost every vote vector it has a unique attractor made of polytopes, and for three parties they construct the invariant polygons and chart how they change across Farey cells. They also show the discrepancy bound stays sharp for fixed vote shares. Results are exact mathematics for the method only and exclude exceptional vote vectors.
items.title: Frege's election method: discrepancy, invariant polygons and Farey geometry

items.hook: For half of the rational values a outside an interval, a maximal second iterate forces all iterates maximal.
items.summary: The paper gives a simpler proof of earlier results on when every iterate of x^2 + a has the largest possible Galois group, and extends them from integers to rational a. For a set of density 1/2 outside a certain interval, checking the second iterate suffices. It was produced with Claude and formalized in Lean, while the fourth-iterate conjecture rests only on experiments.
items.title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?

items.hook: PeV photons from Cygnus X-3 show no Lorentz-violation cutoff, tightening limits nearly tenfold.

readout.label: Highest photon energy from Cygnus X-3

items.summary: LHAASO saw photons up to 3.7 PeV from Cygnus X-3, and the spectrum shows no sharp cutoff that photon decay would cause if light speed varied with energy. That sets the second-order Lorentz violation scale above 10^-2 Planck mass. It covers only superluminal scenarios and one flaring source, and assumes a hard intrinsic spectrum.
items.title: Constraints on Lorentz Invariance Violation from PeV Gamma Rays of Cygnus X-3 Observed by LHAASO

items.hook: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays carry too many heavy nuclei to match any known seed population.
items.hook_turn: to match any known seed population.
items.summary: Fits to Pierre Auger Observatory data, evaluated at fixed rigidity, give two families of composition solutions. Only one lets the source hydrogen abundance match that of low-energy cosmic rays, yet both need an excess of silicon-iron group nuclei. The result depends on the assumed source and propagation models used in the fits.
items.title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays require metal-rich sources

items.hook: A class of mixed-integer linear programs can be solved in strongly polynomial time.
items.summary: The proof covers programs whose constraint matrix is totally unimodular with at most two nonzeros per row. It reduces them to minimizing an L-convex function. The result applies only to this narrow structure, not to mixed-integer programming in general.
items.title: Mixed-integer dual network problems are solvable in strongly polynomial time

items.hook: For any unbounded set, a nearly full-measure closed set exists that contains no affine copy of it.
items.hook_turn: contains no affine copy of it.
items.summary: The paper constructs, for every unbounded set of real numbers and every small epsilon, a closed set that fills at least 1 minus epsilon of every unit interval yet has no nontrivial scaled and shifted copy of that set. This settles the Erdos similarity problem in the large. The full similarity question for bounded sets, such as sequences, stays open.
items.title: A resolution of the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem in the large

items.hook: Mirroring a vision transformer's position code alone flips left-right answers in 84-93% of tests.
items.summary: In three open vision-language models, flipping only the width position code of the image encoder reproduces the answer to a flipped image on most left-right questions in CV-Bench. Mirroring the language model's token positions changes few answers. Results come from three model families and two benchmarks, and the abstract notes that some analyses were run after the fact.
items.title: Where Do Vision-Language Models Get Left and Right? Position-Code Counterfactuals in Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3

items.hook: Moire graphene shows evidence of a self-formed electron crystal with quantized Hall states.
items.summary: Transport and noise measurements in hole-doped moire rhombohedral graphene reveal Chern insulators across a continuous range of densities that do not match the moire lattice. They also show current-induced noise, memory effects and gate hysteresis, pointing to a spontaneously charge-ordered parent state. The evidence is indirect, with no direct imaging of the crystal.
items.title: Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moir\'e rhombohedral graphene

items.hook: Dynamical codes built from measurement sequences are extended to GKP codes, with a lower-weight example.
items.summary: The paper builds a theory of dynamical codes for GKP oscillator qubits, giving a way to compute the syndrome and distance of a measurement sequence. In an example, a two-mode square-hexagonal Floquet code has lower measurement weight than square or hexagonal GKP codes. It is a theoretical framework with no hardware demonstration.
items.title: Dynamical GKP codes

items.hook: Quantum Tanner codes reach erasure-channel capacity with linear distance and a linear-time decoder.
items.summary: The authors prove that tensor products of capacity-achieving classical codes also achieve capacity on the erasure channel, and use such local codes to build binary quantum Tanner codes. These have bounded check weights, distance growing linearly with blocklength, and decoding error that falls exponentially. The results hold for erasure noise only, not for more general noise.
items.title: Classical Tensor Codes and Quantum Tanner Codes Achieve Capacity on Erasure Channels

items.hook: State-dependent diffusion makes equilibrium particles look like they sediment, repel or rotate.
items.hook_turn: look like they sediment, repel or rotate.
items.summary: When diffusion varies with a system's state, the drift measured from trajectories includes a spurious part unrelated to forces. It is identical forward and backward in time, so pairing it with the wrong diffusion tensor makes passive particles look active. The author shows how to infer this part from trajectory moments. The argument is theoretical in the abstract, without an experimental test.
items.title: And yet it moves - or does it? Spurious drifts at equilibrium
